target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: fix(config): reject unsupported MCP disabled config
target.body:
Closes #103954

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators configured an MCP server with `disabled: true` and OpenClaw silently started the server because only `enabled: false` controls MCP activation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change migrates the unsupported inverse flag to the canonical enablement setting through `openclaw doctor --fix`, while configuration validation now reports the incorrect key with an actionable replacement. Runtime behavior continues to read only the canonical setting.

## User Impact

Operators receive a clear configuration error instead of unexpectedly spawning an MCP server. Existing boolean `disabled` entries can be repaired automatically with `openclaw doctor --fix`.

## Evidence

### Real isolated CLI proof

Executed from PR head `f53982039f67` with Node `v24.14.0`, using isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` values and no real credentials. The configured stdio command was `/usr/bin/touch $MARKER`, so any process start would leave an observable marker.

Before repair, `openclaw config validate --json` exited 1 and reported:

```json
{
  "valid": false,
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "mcp.servers.proof-disabled.disabled",
      "message": "unsupported key \"disabled\"; use \"enabled: false\" instead, then run \"openclaw doctor --fix\" to migrate existing config"
    }
  ]
}
```

`openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` exited 0 and printed:

```text
Legacy config keys detected
- mcp.servers uses the unsupported "disabled" key; use "enabled: false" instead.

Doctor changes
Moved mcp.servers.proof-disabled.disabled true → enabled false.

Updated config: $CONFIG
Doctor complete.
```

The rewritten entry contained the canonical field and no `disabled` key:

```json
{
  "enabled": false,
  "command": "/usr/bin/touch",
  "args": ["$MARKER"],
  "transport": "stdio"
}
```

After repair, `openclaw config validate --json` exited 0 with `{"valid":true,"warnings":[]}`.

For the post-repair process-start check, the marker was removed and the actual MCP runtime probe was run:

```console
$ openclaw mcp probe --json
{
  "servers": {},
  "tools": [],
  "diagnostics": []
}
$ test -e "$MARKER" && echo present || echo absent
absent
```

A named probe also rejected the server before launch: `MCP server "proof-disabled" is disabled ... Run openclaw mcp configure proof-disabled --enable before probing it.`

### Contract and automated validation

- OpenClaw filters `mcp.servers` entries with `enabled: false` before session MCP runtime materialization (`src/agents/bundle-mcp-config.ts`).
- Direct upstream Codex source inspection at [`5c19155cbd93`](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/5c19155cbd93bfa099016e7487259f61669823ff) confirmed that `enabled` defaults to true, `false` means skip initialization, and the connection manager filters disabled servers before spawning them (`codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs`, `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/connection_manager.rs`).
- Focused config and doctor tests passed: 237 assertions across the relevant test shards.
- Core TypeScript check passed with `pnpm tsgo:core`.
- Regression coverage verifies both inverse-value migration and preservation of an explicitly configured `enabled` value.

## AI-assisted contribution

Implemented with Codex; targeted tests, core typechecking, direct upstream contract inspection, and isolated real CLI proof were completed before submission.

target.title: fix(exa): cover centralized web search secrets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Exa web search already relies on the centralized runtime web-search SecretRef resolver, but the regression coverage did not lock that contract for Exa specifically. That made it easy for future Exa changes to reintroduce provider-local SecretRef handling or silently bypass configured SecretRefs with `EXA_API_KEY` fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made
This PR adds focused regression coverage for the existing centralized Exa credential path instead of changing Exa runtime behavior. The tests prove Exa participates in the shared web-search SecretRef matrix and that the runtime diagnostics/recovery path stays explicit when a configured Exa SecretRef is unresolved.

## User Impact
Users who configure an Exa web-search SecretRef get coverage that the runtime resolves the configured credential through the shared path. If the configured Exa SecretRef cannot be resolved, the diagnostic/recovery behavior is covered without silently changing provider routing.

## Evidence
- `extensions/exa/src/exa-web-search-provider.test.ts` covers configured Exa API key precedence over ambient `EXA_API_KEY` and the documented `EXA_API_KEY` fallback when no key is configured.
- `src/secrets/runtime-web-tools.test.ts` includes Exa in the shared web-search provider SecretRef matrix.
- `src/secrets/runtime-web-tools.test.ts` covers unresolved Exa SecretRefs plus `EXA_API_KEY` recovery diagnostics.
- Net production behavior is unchanged; `extensions/exa/src/exa-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` still only consumes an already-resolved configured key or `EXA_API_KEY` fallback.

target.title: fix(ollama): resolve web search secret refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Ollama web search had provider-local SecretRef handling for `models.providers.ollama.apiKey`. That duplicated the shared web-search credential contract and made it easier for configured SecretRef behavior to drift from other web-search providers.

## Why This Change Was Made
The Ollama runtime now uses the shared `resolveWebSearchProviderCredential(...)` helper for configured literals, env-backed SecretRefs, unavailable configured refs, and ambient env fallback. Ollama keeps only its provider-specific credential usability filter and stable diagnostic text.

## User Impact
Users who configure an env SecretRef for the Ollama provider key get that resolved key on web-search requests. If the configured SecretRef is missing or non-env, Ollama fails before a network request instead of silently falling through to an unrelated ambient `OLLAMA_API_KEY`. Existing marker-string fallback to `OLLAMA_API_KEY` is preserved.

## Evidence
- `src/agents/tools/web-search-provider-credentials.ts` now supports provider-owned normalization and an unavailable-configured-ref callback while preserving existing fallback behavior for callers that do not opt in.
- `extensions/ollama/src/web-search-provider.ts` no longer imports or calls `resolveSecretInputString`; it delegates the SecretRef/fallback contract to the shared helper.
- `src/agents/tools/web-search-provider-credentials.test.ts` covers env SecretRef success, no ambient fallback for unavailable refs, caller notification for unavailable refs, and marker-string fallback.
- `extensions/ollama/src/web-search-provider.test.ts` covers resolved env SecretRef request auth plus missing/non-env SecretRefs rejecting before `fetchWithSsrFGuard` is called.

target.title: fix: Control UI avatar initial breaks on emoji display names
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI sidebar avatar rendered a broken or garbled initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half / replacement character) instead of the intended glyph.
- Solution: Replaced `(label || agent.id).slice(0, 1).toUpperCase()` (first UTF-16 code unit) with a new `deriveAvatarInitial` helper that uses `String.fromCodePoint(value.codePointAt(0))` (first full code point), returning `""` for empty or missing names.
- What changed: `ui/src/lib/avatar.ts` — new exported `deriveAvatarInitial`; `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` now uses it.
- What did NOT change: Behavior for ordinary ASCII names; other `.slice()` sites were intentionally left unchanged because they operate on ASCII-only inputs (hex UUIDs, commit SHAs, ASCII-stripped build IDs) and are not surrogate-unsafe.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** The avatar initial for emoji-initial display names was a dangling UTF-16 surrogate; it is now the full code point (a single glyph).
- **Real environment tested:** Direct node function call against the patched module on branch `fix/control-ui-avatar-initial-utf16`, using `node --import tsx`; did not boot a full OpenClaw runtime (pure string helper).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx avatar-evidence.ts
  # avatar-evidence.ts imports the exported deriveAvatarInitial and calls it on sample inputs.
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  deriveAvatarInitial("😀Name") = "😀" (expected "😀") OK
  deriveAvatarInitial("🚀") = "🚀" (expected "🚀") OK
  deriveAvatarInitial("Bob") = "B" (expected "B") OK
  deriveAvatarInitial("") = "" (expected "") OK
  deriveAvatarInitial(null) = "" (expected "") OK
  deriveAvatarInitial("  ") = " " (expected " ") OK
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Emoji/astral initials are preserved as a single glyph; ASCII names are uppercased to their first char; empty/null input yields `""`.
- **What was not tested:** Did not start a live OpenClaw UI instance; only exercised the patched `deriveAvatarInitial` function locally (per guide §4 degradation for pure utility functions).

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: emoji-initial name → first code point; ASCII → uppercased first char; empty/null → `""`.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Locks the exact code-point (not code-unit) contract that the sidebar renders, which is the precise defect.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: The avatar initial used `.slice(0, 1)`, which takes the first UTF-16 code unit. An astral code point such as an emoji occupies two code units, so the slice split it in half and yielded a dangling surrogate.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No code-point-aware initial-derivation helper.

target.title: fix: bound ed25519 base64url decode input length
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `base64UrlDecode` in `src/infra/ed25519-signature.ts` previously decoded any input length into a `Buffer`, so a caller could pass an arbitrarily large string and force large memory allocation per request. These inputs flow from attacker-influenced values (public keys / signatures in device-identity and auth paths).
- Solution: Added `MAX_BASE64URL_DECODE_INPUT_LENGTH = 4096` and reject oversized input with a thrown error before decoding. Every real caller passes fixed-size ed25519 public keys, private keys, or signatures (≤ ~86 base64url chars), so 4096 is vastly generous and cannot affect legitimate use. The existing callers already wrap `base64UrlDecode` in `try/catch` (returning `null`/`false`), so the new throw is safely absorbed as a parse failure rather than a crash.
- What changed: `src/infra/ed25519-signature.ts` — `base64UrlDecode` now rejects input longer than the bound.
- What did NOT change: Valid key/signature decoding behavior; the error-handling contract (callers already treat a throw as a decode failure).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Unbounded base64url decode could allocate arbitrary memory on attacker-influenced input; it is now bounded at 4096 characters.
- **Real environment tested:** Direct node function call against the patched module on branch `fix/ed25519-base64-length`, using `node --import tsx`; did not boot a full OpenClaw runtime (pure decode helper).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx ed25519-evidence.ts
  # ed25519-evidence.ts decodes a valid 32-byte key and a 5000-char input via base64UrlDecode.
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  valid 32-byte key -> decoded length = 32 (expected 32) OK
  oversized 5000-char input -> throws: base64url input exceeds the maximum allowed length
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Valid keys decode to 32 bytes; oversized input throws before any large allocation.
- **What was not tested:** Did not start a live OpenClaw instance or exercise device-identity/auth paths end-to-end; only exercised the patched `base64UrlDecode` function locally (per guide §4 degradation for pure utility functions).

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `src/infra/ed25519-signature.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: fixed-size key → 32 bytes; 5000-char input → throws `/maximum allowed length/`.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Locks the exact length-guard contract at the decode entry point, which is the precise defect.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: `base64UrlDecode` performed no input-length bound before `Buffer.from`, allowing unbounded allocation on malformed or abusive input.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No maximum-input-length check on the decode entry point.

target.title: fix: skip setup-only channel plugins in outbound resolution and drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect
target.body:
## Summary

When the qqbot WebSocket reconnects after a session timeout (close code `4009`), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returns a setup-only plugin stub that lacks any send capability. This causes the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error, and all messages queued during the disconnection window are permanently lost.

## Root Cause

`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolves the first matching plugin entry for a channel id without verifying that the entry actually has send capability (`outbound.sendText`, `message.send.text`, etc.). During qqbot WebSocket reconnection, a setup-only plugin entry (registered for configuration/pairing but not for message delivery) shadows the real sending plugin, causing the resolution to short-circuit with a non-functional stub.

Regression introduced in 2026.5.28 (commit `e932160`).

## Fix

### 1. Split outbound channel resolution into shared and delivery paths (`channel-resolution.ts`)

Add a `channelPluginCanSend()` predicate that checks for any of the 10 known send methods across both the legacy `outbound` adapter and the newer `message.send` adapter:

- `outbound.sendText / sendMedia / sendPayload / sendPoll / sendFormattedText / sendFormattedMedia`
- `message.send.text / media / payload / poll`

Instead of gating the shared `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolver (which would break action-only channel plugins that have `actions.handleAction` but no send capability), a new **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`** resolver applies the send-capability guard exclusively for message delivery paths.

- **`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`**: Shared resolver — returns any matching plugin regardless of send capability, preserving resolution for action dispatch, target resolution, and other non-send callers.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`**: Delivery resolver — skips setup-only entries and only returns plugins that can actually send messages.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter()`**: Updated to use the delivery resolver.
- **`message.ts`**: `sendMessage`/`sendPoll` updated to use the delivery resolver.

### 2. Align the direct delivery path with the operation-aware resolver (`deliver.ts`)

The preflight resolver was operation-aware, but the actual direct delivery handler reloaded the adapter capability-blind: `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` → `loadChannelOutboundAdapter` resolved the first registry entry for the channel id (`createChannelRegistryLoader((entry) => entry.plugin.outbound)`) without checking send capability. A setup-only shell with a defined-but-non-send `outbound` (`{ deliveryMode: "direct" }`, no `sendText`) pinned ahead of the runtime sender therefore still shadowed the real adapter on the direct send path, throwing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` even after preflight had selected a valid plugin. This also affected the reconnect drain path, which has no preflight.

`loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now resolves through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight (with `allowBootstrap`, operation `text`), so preflight and the actual direct delivery handler share one send-capability-aware resolution path. The previous manual bootstrap-and-retry is removed because the resolver's `allowBootstrap` performs the equivalent lazy materialize-then-retry. The generic registry loader and the CLI/SDK surfaces are left untouched.

### 3. Drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect (`extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts`)

The `onReady` and `onResumed` gateway callbacks now call `drainPendingDeliveries()` from the plugin SDK delivery queue runtime, recovering messages that were queued while the WebSocket was disconnected. The drain is:

- Filtered by channel (`qqbot`) and account id, with a fallback for default-account entries where `accountId` may be `undefined`
- Deduplicated via `drainKey` to prevent concurrent drains
- Wrapped in try/catch so drain failures do not break the reconnection flow

### 4. Route the gateway poll handler through the operation-aware resolver (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`)

The gateway `poll` handler still resolved its outbound plugin via the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, while `sendPoll` (`message.ts`) and the direct text delivery path (`deliver.ts`) already routed through the operation-aware `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`. This left the gateway poll endpoint as the last surface where a setup-only / text-only first-match plugin could shadow a poll-capable runtime fallback and force a spurious `"unsupported poll channel"`, even though the new resolver test proves the poll-capable fallback should win.

The poll handler now resolves through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, mirroring the text delivery path. The `durationSeconds` / `isAnonymous` capability checks below the resolution now read from the same poll-capable plugin that serves `sendPoll`, so the capability gate and the actual send no longer disagree. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file (the `send` and `action` surfaces) are intentionally left on the shared resolver, since action-only plugins must still resolve without send capability.

## Tests

- `channel-resolution.test.ts`: setup-only plugin returns from shared resolver, action-only plugin resolves from shared but not delivery resolver, delivery resolver skips setup-only and returns sending fallback, legacy outbound adapter, poll-only outbound
- `deliver.test.ts`: new unmocked regression driving the real `deliverOutboundPayloads` → `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` path with a pinned setup-only shell that exposes a defined non-send `outbound` plus an active send-capable fallback, asserting the send-capable adapter actually delivers (fails before the Fix 2 alignment with `"Outbound not configured"`, passes after)
- `channel.test.ts`: onReady drain, onResumed drain

Fixes #88955.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: After a QQ Bot WebSocket disconnect (session takeover / close code 4009), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returned a setup-only plugin stub instead of the runtime entry, causing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` and dropping all pending deliveries.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw `2026.6.2` (commit `b90683e`, branch `fix/qqbot-reconnect-outbound-88955`), macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. QQ Bot plugin `@openclaw/qqbot@2026.5.31-beta.4` with live QQ Bot credentials (appId `<redacted>`).

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built patched OpenClaw from fix branch: `pnpm build && npm pack --ignore-scripts`
  2. Installed globally: `npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz` — confirmed version: `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)`
  3. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  4. Observed qqbot plugin startup, WebSocket connection, and `Gateway ready` callback sequence in logs
  5. Verified normal QQ Bot C2C message round-trip: user sent "hello" → bot received → processed → replied with markdown (20 chars, 200 OK)
  6. Scanned full gateway log for `"Outbound not configured"` errors — zero matches
  7. Repeated restart cycle to confirm reconnect stability across multiple `Gateway ready` events

- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  # Patched OpenClaw installed and running
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)

  # Gateway restart sequence — qqbot reconnects cleanly
  2026-06-02T22:38:53.727+08:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; restarting
  2026-06-02T22:39:15.986+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.6s)
  2026-06-02T22:39:16.171+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Starting gateway — appId=<redacted>, enabled=true
  2026-06-02T22:39:17.387+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Connecting to wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.468+08:00 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.641+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready

  # Successful QQ Bot message delivery after reconnect
  2026-06-02T22:32:40.229+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Processing message from <redacted>: hello
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.431+08:00 [qqbot] [default] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.432+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Sent markdown chunk (20/20 chars) with 0 HTTP images (c2c)

  # Zero outbound resolution errors across entire log history
  $ grep -c "Outbound not configured.*qqbot" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log
  0

  # Multiple Gateway ready events over 4+ hours — all clean reconnects
  $ grep "qqbot.*Gateway ready" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log | wc -l
  18
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: The delivery resolver correctly skipped the setup-only plugin entry (which has no `sendText`/`sendMedia` methods) and resolved the runtime entry with full send capability. Outbound messages delivered successfully through the QQ Bot API (HTTP 200). Zero occurrences of the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error across 18 reconnect cycles over a 4+ hour observation window. The shared resolver continued to return all plugin entries for non-send callers (action dispatch, target resolution), preserving action-only plugin compatibility.

- **Direct delivery path alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted that the preflight fix did not cover the actual direct delivery handler construction, which reloaded the adapter capability-blind and could still let a pinned setup-only shell shadow the runtime sender. `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now routes through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): the new unmocked `deliver.test.ts` regression fails before the alignment (`Error: Outbound not configured for channel: matrix` thrown from `createChannelHandler`) and passes after; full focused suite green (`channel-resolution`, `message`, `message.channels`, `deliver`, qqbot `channel` — 169 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean, `pnpm build` clean, `git diff --check` clean, lint clean.

- **Gateway poll resolver alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted the gateway poll endpoint (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) still used the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, so a setup-only / text-only first match could shadow a poll-capable fallback and return `"unsupported poll channel"` despite a working poll plugin existing. The poll handler now routes through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, matching `sendPoll` and the direct text delivery path. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): a new gateway `send.test.ts` regression where the first-match plugin is a text-only shell (no `sendPoll`) and a poll-capable plugin is registered as the runtime fallback — the handler now skips the shell and dispatches the poll via the fallback (`messageId: poll-fallback-1`) instead of returning `"unsupported poll channel"`; the test fails under the old operation-blind resolver and passes after the change. Full gateway send suite green (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` — 124 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file are intentionally untouched.

- **What was not tested**:

  Live drain proof is not reproducible on the fixed build. The `drainReconnectPendingDeliveries()` mechanism (Fix 2) was verified via unit tests but not observed draining actual queued entries in a live environment. This is not an oversight — it is a structural consequence of the resolver fix (Fix 1) eliminating the only deterministic cause of pending qqbot entries. Code-level analysis confirms this:

  **How the delivery queue works** (`deliver.ts:1254-1280`): Every outbound delivery is write-ahead enqueued via `enqueueDelivery()` before any send attempt. On success, `ackDelivery()` removes the entry (`deliver.ts:1367`). On throw, `failDelivery()` bumps `retryCount` and **leaves it pending** (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:137-144`).

  **What created the pending entries in #88955**: The `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` throw fired from `createChannelHandler` (`deliver.ts:223-231`) when `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery` returned a setup-only plugin with no send methods. This throw occurs **outside** the per-payload try/catch (`deliver.ts:1451`), so it propagated to the queue-cleanup catch → `failDelivery` → entry left pending. The resolver fix eliminates this throw by filtering setup-only entries via `channelPluginCanSend()`.

  **Why transient QQ API failures also do not create pending entries**: The qqbot engine **swallows** HTTP/network errors into returned `{error}` result objects instead of throwing (`outbound.ts:301-304, 313-318`). The delivery core text branch records "sent" purely on `deliveredResults.length > 0` with no message-id identity gate (`deliver.ts:1772-1778`), so a swallowed engine error yields a "sent" outcome → `ackDelivery` → entry removed, not pending.

  **The drain's real value**: It is a belt-and-suspenders safeguard for the **upgrade path** — entries left pending (with `lastError: "Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`) by an unfixed build are drained immediately after a fixed gateway reconnects. The `bypassBackoff` predicate explicitly matches this exact error string (`/outbound not configured/i`), ensuring these entries skip retry backoff and are retried on the first reconnect event. If the retry still fails (e.g., the plugin is genuinely misconfigured), `isPermanentDeliveryError` (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:79`) moves the entry to `failed/` — no infinite retry loop. `MAX_RETRIES` is also enforced before the bypass branch (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:544`). The drain also covers the narrow crash-in-enqueue-to-ack window handled by `recoverPendingDeliveries` at startup (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`). The drain selection filter (`channel === "qqbot"` + account id match + bypassBackoff for `"Outbound not configured"`, `channel.test.ts:90-152`) and the reconnect-drain integration logic (`delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`) are exercised by 35 unit tests (all passing).

  **Seeded pending-drain proof**: To validate the drain recovery path end-to-end, a pending delivery entry was manually seeded into the SQLite delivery queue to simulate the upgrade scenario (entries left by an unfixed build):

  1. Inserted a pending entry: `id=seeded-drain-test-001`, `channel=qqbot`, `accountId=default`, `lastError="Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`, `retry_count=1`
  2. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Observed recovery sequence in logs:

  ```
  00:30:00.353 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.9s)
  00:30:00.987 [delivery-recovery] Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
  00:30:01.567 [qqbot] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Recovered delivery seeded-drain-test-001 on qqbot
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
  00:30:02.816 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  00:30:02.952 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready
  ```

  4. Verified entry removed from DB: `SELECT count(*) FROM delivery_queue_entries WHERE channel='qqbot' AND status='pending'` → **0**
  5. Zero `"Outbound not configured"` errors after restart

  **Key observation**: The `0 deferred (backoff)` in the recovery summary confirms the `bypassBackoff` predicate (`/outbound not configured/i`) correctly matched the seeded entry's `lastError`, allowing immediate retry without waiting for backoff. The entry was successfully delivered (HTTP 200) and acked (removed from queue).

  **Note**: The startup `recoverPendingDeliveries` path (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`) executed before the qqbot `onReady` callback (`00:30:00.987` vs `00:30:02.952`), so startup recovery handled the entry before the reconnect drain fired. Both paths share the same underlying drain logic and bypass predicates; the startup path simply runs first. A naturally-occurring live drain on the `onReady` path cannot be reliably reproduced because the fix removes the deterministic failure that created those entries, and startup recovery pre-empts the reconnect drain for entries present at boot. Multi-shard configurations were not tested.

target.title: fix: ClawHub search passes unbounded limit to the API
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: The shared ClawHub search helpers `searchClawHubPackages` and `searchClawHubSkills` forward the caller-supplied `limit` verbatim to the ClawHub API. Direct callers (the `skills search` CLI flag, plugin catalog search paths) can pass an arbitrarily large value, driving excessive upstream requests, oversized responses, and client memory pressure. The plugin-layer caller already clamps to `MAX_PLUGIN_SEARCH_LIMIT`, but the shared infra functions themselves had no bound.
- Solution: Add a defense-in-depth upper bound at the infra layer: `CLAWHUB_SEARCH_MAX_LIMIT = 100` applied through `clampClawHubSearchLimit` on both search functions, preserving the existing "no limit ⇒ server default" behavior (an unset limit stays unset).
- What changed: `src/infra/clawhub.ts` — new `CLAWHUB_SEARCH_MAX_LIMIT` const and `clampClawHubSearchLimit` helper; non-positive / non-finite limits are treated as unset rather than forwarded.
- What did NOT change: No observable change for callers that pass a valid or omitted limit; the plugin-layer `MAX_PLUGIN_SEARCH_LIMIT = 100` behavior is unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Unbounded `limit` was passed through to the ClawHub search API; it is now capped at 100 while preserving the server default when unset.
- **Real environment tested:** Direct node function call against the patched module on branch `fix/clawhub-search-limit-cap`, using `node --import tsx`; did not boot a full OpenClaw runtime (pure input-boundary helper).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx clawhub-evidence.ts
  # clawhub-evidence.ts calls the public searchClawHubPackages API with a mock
  # fetchImpl that captures the real request URL (including the limit query param).
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  limit=999999 -> request limit param = 100
  limit=5 -> request limit param = 5
  limit=-3 (non-positive) -> request limit param = (omitted)
  limit=undefined (omitted) -> request limit param = (omitted)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Values above 100 are clamped to 100; 5 passes through as 5; non-positive and undefined limits are omitted so the server default applies.
- **What was not tested:** Did not start a live OpenClaw instance or hit the real ClawHub endpoint; only exercised the patched `clampClawHubSearchLimit` path through the public `searchClawHubPackages` API with a mock fetch (per guide §4 degradation for pure utility functions).

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `src/infra/clawhub.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: `limit: 999999` → request URL `limit=100`; `limit: 5` → `limit=5`; no `limit` → param omitted.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Asserts the exact query-param contract the API receives, covering the overflow, pass-through, and omit paths in one helper.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: The shared infra search helpers had no input bound on `limit`; any direct caller could request an unbounded number of results.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No clamp at the infra layer — the plugin caller's `MAX_PLUGIN_SEARCH_LIMIT` only covered one path, leaving the shared functions unprotected.

target.title: refactor(whatsapp): use runtime context for connection controllers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp maintained a process-global connection-controller registry alongside the channel runtime-context registry already provided by the Plugin SDK. That parallel state owner made controller discovery a WhatsApp-specific lifecycle concern and created another registry path that could drift from the shared channel runtime model.

This is a maintainer-requested refactor. No linked issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

Connection controllers are now published through `registerChannelRuntimeContext` and resolved through `getChannelRuntimeContext`, keyed by WhatsApp account and the `connection-controller` capability. The plugin-injected channel runtime is the canonical owner because outbound adapters, agent tools, active-listener checks, and reconnect handoff readers can execute outside the gateway account task.

The SDK lease replaces the custom unregister path. Ready replacements are published before stale leases are disposed, preserving uninterrupted lookup while the SDK token contract prevents an old lease from unregistering its successor.

The old registry implementation, unregister API, and duplicate-module registry test are deleted rather than retained as compatibility layers.

## User Impact

There is no intended user-visible behavior change. WhatsApp sends, delivery recovery, call-tool identity lookup, active-listener checks, and reconnect successor handoff continue to resolve the live controller, now through the shared Plugin SDK runtime-context seam.

This reduces lifecycle duplication and makes future runtime-context behavior consistent with other channel capabilities.

## Evidence

- Hosted focused WhatsApp tests passed for controller lifecycle, active-listener lookup, outbound delivery, call-tool identity lookup, and reconnect successor handoff.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed, including extension production/test typechecks, formatting, lint, boundary guards, and runtime import-cycle validation.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Structured Codex autoreview: clean, with no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix: complete C1 control-character (0x80-0x9f) coverage across terminal/log sinks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Terminal-control sanitization across the codebase guards untrusted text before it reaches a terminal or log, preventing ANSI escape / log-forging injection (CWE-117). The canonical range is C0 (0x00–0x1f), DEL (0x7f), **and C1 (0x80–0x9f)** — the range already used by the shared `sanitizeForLog` in `packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts` and by `renderTerminalBufferText` (merged in #103274). The C1 range includes the 8-bit CSI introducer **U+009B** (equivalent to `ESC [`).

Several output sinks had drifted: they covered C0/DEL but not C1, so a C1 byte (e.g. U+009B) passed through into terminal/log output. Rather than land these as isolated one-sink patches (per maintainer feedback on #103226), this is a single **deliberate, sink-wide pass**: it audits every control-character sink, closes the C1 gap in the terminal/log output sinks, and documents why the remaining sinks are already covered, out of scope, or deferred.

## Sink-wide audit

### ① Fixed here — C1 added to terminal/log output sinks (each with a focused regression test)

| Sink (function) | File | Action on control chars |
|---|---|---|
| `hasControlCharacter` (gates `buildProviderReauthCommand`) | `src/agents/failover-error.ts` | reject (suppress command) |
| `sanitizeModelWarningValue` | `src/agents/model-selection-shared.ts` | truncate at first control |
| `hasUnsafeControlChars` | `src/agents/sandbox/runtime-status.ts` | gate (agent-only fallback) |
| `escapeControlCharsVisible` | `src/agents/tool-policy-audit.ts` | escape → `\xNN` |
| `validateAttachmentName` + `describeRejectedName` | `src/agents/subagent-attachments.ts` | reject + escape diagnostic |
| `sanitizeInlineDirectiveText` | `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.ts` | escape → `\uNNNN` |
| `scrubDoctorErrorMessage` | `src/flows/doctor-error-message.ts` | strip |
| `sanitizeLookupPathForLog` | `src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts` | replace → `?` |
| `sanitizeForConsole` | `src/agents/console-sanitize.ts` | strip |
| `escapeControlCharsForTerminal` | `src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.ts` | escape → `\xNN` |
| `replaceLogControlCharacters` (via `formatHookErrorForLog`) | `src/hooks/fire-and-forget.ts` | replace → space |
| `formatDiagnosticValue` | `src/infra/restart-handoff.ts` | replace → space |

Each keeps its own action; only the control-code classification is aligned with `sanitizeForLog`'s range. **Why not just call `sanitizeForLog`?** It strips *all* control + ANSI *and* removes tabs/newlines, and lacks these sinks' semantics — visible escaping, `?` replacement, boundary truncation, rejection, whitespace-flattening, length caps, and optional-value handling. The right boundary is the local predicate at each sink; this PR only completes the shared range there.

### ② Already C1-complete (unchanged, referenced for coverage)

- `sanitizeForLog` — `packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts` (canonical range).
- `renderTerminalBufferText` — `src/gateway/terminal/buffer-text.ts` (#103274, merged).

### ③ In-scope but deferred

- `sanitizeHookConsoleValue` — `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`. A console-warning sink that is genuinely in scope, but its only caller is inside the full gateway hook request handler; it warrants dedicated integration coverage. Deferred to a follow-up rather than shipping an untested one-liner here.

### ④ Considered and excluded (different threat model — not terminal/log output injection)

- `hasPromptUnsafeControlCharacter` — `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts`: no-op for C1; the immediately-following ASCII allowlist already rejects it (this was #103401, closed).
- `stripDisallowedChatControlChars` — `src/gateway/chat-input-sanitize.ts`: chat-message **input** sanitization routed to channels; tab/LF/CR intentionally preserved.
- `sanitizeMediaDirectiveValue` — `src/agents/internal-events.ts`: builds prompt/runtime-context text, not terminal output.
- `sanitizeArgs` — `src/plugins/commands.ts`; `stripControlChars` — `src/cli/windows-argv.ts`: argv/plugin-arg normalization (input side).
- Input/URL/JSON-validity validators (`validateNoControlChars` in acp, `hasControlOrWhitespace` in scp-host, `normalizeProviderFinalUrl` in web-fetch, `isControlCharacter` in `packages/ai` JSON escaping) — reject/validate for other reasons; C1 is not an ANSI-injection concern there.

## Testing / Proof

All twelve fixed sinks have a focused regression using a **valid** U+009B sequence (CSI + `31m`, since U+009B is itself the complete introducer — no extra `[`). Per-file `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file>` results:

| Test file | Result |
|---|---|
| `agents/failover-error.test.ts` | 98 passed (incl. C1 provider-id rejection) |
| `agents/model-selection-shared.test.ts` | 2 passed (C1 boundary truncation) |
| `agents/sandbox-explain.test.ts` | 6 passed (session-label escaping + agent-only fallback) |
| `agents/subagent-attachments.test.ts` | 3 passed (C1 name rejected + escaped diagnostic) |
| `agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts` | 57 passed |
| `agents/console-sanitize.test.ts` | 3 passed |
| `commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts` | 33 passed (+1 skipped) |
| `flows/doctor-error-message.test.ts` | 4 passed |
| `hooks/fire-and-forget.test.ts` | 6 passed (`formatHookErrorForLog`) |
| `infra/restart-handoff.test.ts` | 11 passed |
| `gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts` | new C1 test passes ✅ (see note) |

> Note on `config.test.ts`: four sibling `config.openFile` tests hard-code POSIX `/tmp/...` paths and assert the full path string. On my local **Windows** checkout the handler resolves those to `D:\tmp\...`, so they fail identically on `main` (unrelated to this change) and pass on Linux CI. The new `replaces C1 control characters in the logged failed config path` test deliberately asserts only the sanitized `cfg?.json` fragment, so it is green on both platforms.

Real code-point evidence (before → after) for `sanitizeModelWarningValue`, toggling only the one-line predicate: on current `main` a providerless model `gpt4<U+0080>EVIL` logs `Model "gpt4EVIL" ...` (residual C1 dropped, attacker suffix retained); with this change it logs `Model "gpt4" ...` (truncated at the C1 boundary).

## Relationship to the open C1 PRs

This supersedes the seven isolated sink PRs (#103379 #103380 #103381 #103382 #103383 #103402 #103405) and re-lands the `sanitizeForConsole` fix from the closed #103226 cleanly (valid U+009B test, no proof-only scripts). Those PRs will be closed in favor of this consolidated review.

target.title: fix(hooks): report agent startup admission failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/hooks/agent` could return HTTP success as soon as an isolated agent run was queued, even if the run failed before reaching runner-entry/session admission. For Symphony Kanban this made a hook dispatch look durable while the worker had actually hit a lifecycle/startup failure such as:

`Session "agent:herbert-karajan:hook:symphony-kanban" changed while starting work. Retry.`

That left the board with an accepted dispatch but no reliable worker closeout path.

This PR changes agent hook dispatch so startup/admission failures surface through the HTTP response before the idempotency key is cached:

- waits for `onExecutionStarted` before returning `{ ok: true, runId }`
- returns `409` for changed/deleted/archived session startup failures
- returns `503` if runner entry does not start before the admission timeout
- returns `502` for other pre-start failures
- keeps post-start failures on the existing async/log/system-event path
- preserves hook session-key policy and `deliver:false` behavior

## Evidence

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/gateway/hooks.test.ts src/gateway/hooks-mapping.test.ts src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts src/gateway/server-http.hooks-request-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server/hooks.agent-trust.test.ts`
  - passed: 16 files / 314 tests
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
  - passed
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
  - passed

## Operational Boundary

This is source-only. It does not restart or modify any live gateway config by itself. Runtime activation still requires the normal deployment path and an approved gateway refresh.

## Related Tracking

- KAN-278: implementation card for the hook-session routing/admission fix.
- KAN-223: live worker smoke target after merge/deploy/gateway refresh.
- KAN-267: superseded duplicate investigation card.

target.title: fix(tlon): send fragment image URLs as media
target.body:
Related: #104852

AI-assisted PR. I reviewed the diff and focused validation output.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon users sending image media URLs with fragment suffixes, such as `https://cdn.example/image.png#preview`, would have those URLs classified as ordinary links instead of image blocks.

The outbound media story path already treats plain image URLs and image URLs with query strings as image blocks. Fragment-bearing image URLs were the missing sibling case.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change keeps the fix inside Tlon's local image URL classifier by allowing the image extension check to accept either `?query` or `#fragment` suffixes.

This does not change upload behavior, URL fetching, auth, gateway routing, persisted state, migrations, schema, upgrade behavior, or non-image URL handling. It only affects the final Tlon story classification branch for URLs whose path already ends in a known image extension.

## User Impact

Tlon users can now send image URLs that include fragments and still get the expected image media block instead of a plain clickable link when the Tlon send path builds a story from that URL.

For example, `https://cdn.example/image.png#preview` now follows the same media story classification path as `https://cdn.example/image.png` and `https://cdn.example/image.png?token=1`.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the focused local probe showed the mismatch:

```text
https://cdn.example/a.png          => true
https://cdn.example/a.png?token=1  => true
https://cdn.example/a.png#preview  => false
https://cdn.example/a.webp#v=1     => false
```

The focused regression test covers `buildMediaStory("caption", "https://cdn.example/image.png#preview")` and asserts that the URL is emitted as a `block.image` story verse instead of a link verse.

Reviewer-requested live proof is still pending. ClawSweeper asked for redacted evidence from a real Tlon setup showing the upload-fallback path preserves a `.png#fragment` URL and that Tlon renders it as image media. I have not claimed that live proof yet because this machine does not currently have Tlon ship credentials, a login code, or a configured target DM/group channel available.

When a real test setup is available, the intended proof should capture this path:

```text
sendMedia(mediaUrl: "https://[redacted]/image.png#preview")
→ uploadImageFromUrl(mediaUrl)
→ upload fallback returns the original fragment URL
→ buildMediaStory(text, fallbackUrl)
→ Urbit poke payload contains block.image.src
→ Tlon UI renders the message as image media, not a plain link
```

The redacted proof should preserve the `.png#preview` shape and `block.image.src` structure while hiding ship names, login code, cookies, private hosts, request IDs, channel identifiers, and credentials.

## Possible call chain / impact

The relevant source-level fallback chain is:

```text
extensions/tlon/src/channel.runtime.ts sendMedia
→ extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.ts uploadImageFromUrl
→ on upload failure, return the original imageUrl
→ extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.ts buildMediaStory
→ extensions/tlon/src/urbit/story.ts isImageUrl
→ createImageBlock or createLinkInline
```

This PR only changes the Tlon-local classifier used by that story-building branch. Sibling behavior for plain image URLs, query-suffixed image URLs, upload success, auth, routing, and non-image URLs is intentionally unchanged.

## Validation

```text
git diff --check
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.test.ts
```

Result:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       3 passed (3)
```

- Updated direct reply-agent delivery checks to treat visible message-tool sends as delivered only when they match the source route/dedupe criteria.

target.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived embedded sessions could lose prompt-cache reuse when the same session crossed room-event delivery, sender-policy, queue, compaction, recovery, or native Responses continuation boundaries.

The failure was not one cache knob. Turn-specific delivery and authorization changed reusable prompt/tool shape, reconstructed runs could drop authoritative state, and authenticated OpenAI Responses could miss native continuation.

## What Changed

- Keeps the model-visible prompt and ordered tool catalogue stable across owner, non-owner, trusted-internal, unknown-sender, and ambient room-event turns.
- Resolves one deterministic `ToolAccessPolicy` per turn and emits a trusted full snapshot only when permissions change or model state is uncertain.
- Denies unavailable `computer`, `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes` calls with non-retryable `TOOL_ACCESS_DENIED` before hooks, implementations, or side effects.
- Carries immutable policy through loopback MCP grants; request headers cannot widen authority, and current-main capability/revocation checks remain intact.
- Keeps trusted-internal turns non-owner (`senderIsOwner: false`): policy can grant only the four protected core tools without exposing owner-only plugin tools.
- Separates actual reply delivery from the session-stable prompt-facing delivery mode, including `message_tool_only` room events.
- Preserves an explicit forced `message` tool on automatic Codex turns while keeping `disableMessageTool` as the hard veto.
- Propagates policy, owner identity, delivery modes, and forced snapshots through direct, queued, memory, preflight, manual, timeout, overflow, and after-turn compaction paths.
- Acknowledges policy persistence at provider-native durable boundaries for OpenClaw, Codex, and Copilot, with generation checks preventing stale acknowledgements from clearing newer state.
- Preserves native Codex supervision settings while appending trusted turn guidance as a developer history item before the user turn; no model, effort, personality, or collaboration-mode override is introduced.
- Routes built-in authenticated GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 Responses streams through native `previous_response_id` continuation with delta input. Custom streams keep their existing routing.

The earlier experimental post-history developer-message split is not included; that request shape produced HTTP 400 responses on ChatGPT/Codex Responses. Native continuation is fixed through stream classification instead.

## Security And Compatibility

- Tool visibility is not authority. Every protected call is checked again against the immutable current-turn policy immediately before execution.
- Runtime-owned `cron`, `heartbeat`, and `memory` turns are distinct from unknown and explicit non-owner senders. Ambient room-event policy remains fail-closed.
- The model-facing tool-name hash omits turn-specific owner state; the runtime grant retains the effective decision.
- No persistent storage schema or migration is introduced.
- No private sender, channel, account, host, endpoint, credential, or raw trace identifiers are included.

## Evidence

The original same-session reproduction showed the model-visible inventory flipping between 44 and 47 tools, matching prompt/tool digest changes, and cached prefixes collapsing to roughly 2k-10k tokens or ceilinging around 37k-40k.

Numeric-only usage records from a long-lived room session after the stable-shape change show the cached prefix growing from 104,960 to 157,184 tokens. Its final four consecutive provider turns reported `cacheRead` 155,136 / 155,136 / 156,160 / 157,184 with uncached input 1,193 / 1,836 / 2,097 / 1,324, or 98.7-99.2% prefix reuse. Message text, sender/channel/session IDs, hosts, and credentials were excluded.

The exact candidate head was then exercised through isolated, non-delivered live-provider sessions:

- GPT-5.5: cold `input=41,110 cacheRead=0`; warm turns `input=186 cacheRead=40,960` and `input=222 cacheRead=40,960` (99.5% reuse).
- GPT-5.6 Sol: cold `input=41,104 cacheRead=0`; warm turns `input=692 cacheRead=40,448` and `input=728 cacheRead=40,448` (98.2-98.3% reuse).
- The system-prompt hash stayed constant within each model, the ordered catalogue remained 48 tools, and the aggregate ordered tool name/summary/schema digest was identical across warm turns and both models: `a66a993fb1099d80fd84f809b1d3ae408a7ed206d7b7598680c1563ae1d24a65`.

An exact-head focused proof run selected 14 assertions across 18 project suites with zero failures. It verifies room events remain contextual and `message_tool_only`, unauthorized non-owner and ambient calls return non-retryable `TOOL_ACCESS_DENIED` before hooks or implementation, trusted-internal calls execute, and GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 send `previous_response_id` with delta-only input across unchanged and changed policy snapshots.

The exact candidate head is now built and running on the reporter's local gateway. The LaunchAgent uses the repo-local `dist/index.js`, runtime and RPC probes are healthy, the loopback dashboard returns HTTP 200, and `dist/build-info.json` reports the exact commit below.

## Exact-Head Validation

Candidate: `d8b5a47831ba8923114a6cd625a39a8ca3139cae`

Upstream included in branch and used for merge-tree proof: `7027d2c227281d814266311bebab7581b899d6dc`

- merge-tree check against the latest fetched upstream is clean;
- pre-refresh broad validation passed 2,446 changed-file tests across unit-fast, unit, gateway, auto-reply, agents, Codex, and extension shards, including all 86 loopback MCP tests in their owning gateway-server shard;
- exact-head proof passed 14 selected assertions across 18 suites with zero failures;
- exact-head Codex lifecycle, binding, and login-profile compatibility passed 215 tests;

- focused CLI preparation tests confirm trusted-internal policy is preserved while owner identity remains false;
- prior focused suites passed 173 compaction/overflow, 98 harness-selection, and 15 manual-compaction propagation tests;
- prompt snapshots are current;

- `pnpm check:test-types` passed;
- `pnpm lint:core` and `pnpm lint:extensions` passed;

- exact local install: OpenClaw `2026.7.2`, LaunchAgent loaded, runtime active, connectivity probe OK, HTTP 200, build-info commit matches candidate, Discord probe OK, and WhatsApp linked/healthy.

The merge also resolves current-main changes to Codex native supervision, ring-zero tool composition, model-lock compaction, Computer Use health probes, and generated prompt snapshots without dropping either side's behavior.

Long-lived embedded sessions can lose provider prompt-cache reuse when adjacent turns cross room-event delivery, authorization, queue, compaction, recovery, or native Responses continuation boundaries.

Sanitized same-session traces showed model-visible tool inventory changing between 44 and 47 tools, prompt/tool digests changing with it, and cached prefixes collapsing to roughly 2k-10k tokens or plateauing around 37k-40k.

## Root Cause

Three independent concerns were coupled:

1. turn-specific delivery and authorization changed reusable prompt/tool definitions;
2. reconstructed queue, memory, compaction, fallback, and recovery runs could lose authoritative state;

- Supervised Codex turns keep native model/effort/personality settings while receiving trusted turn guidance through append-only developer history.

target.title: fix(cli): abort reaps autonomous executor process trees
target.body:
Closes #104847

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where aborting a CLI-backed agent turn on a service-managed Gateway could stop the visible turn while leaving child processes spawned by the autonomous executor alive. Those survivors could continue acting with the executor's credentials after the operator believed the run had stopped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process supervisor now requires callers to declare a typed process role:

- `executor` runs own an independently cancellable process group on POSIX, including service-managed Gateways. If an isolated group cannot be created, startup fails closed instead of falling back to the Gateway's process group.
- `background` runs preserve the existing daemon/service ownership used by `exec`/`process` sessions and cron exit watchers that may intentionally outlive the initiating turn.

Both one-shot CLI backend runs and Claude stdio live sessions are marked as executors. The existing chat-abort path already cancels their managed run; this change makes that cancellation reach the executor's child process hierarchy without signaling the Gateway or changing persistent background-session behavior.

## User Impact

Operators can rely on abort to terminate the active CLI executor and its child process hierarchy. Persistent `exec`/`process` background sessions keep their current lifecycle and continue until they exit or are explicitly stopped.

## Evidence

PR checks for the current head (`0119396a1e`) are running with no patch-related failures at submission time: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104929/checks

Manual full CI dispatch for the same head: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29178217948

Focused coverage added:

- `src/process/supervisor/turn-lifecycle.test.ts` starts a real parent/child process hierarchy under the service-managed marker, cancels the executor run, and verifies both PIDs are gone.
- `src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts` verifies executors still receive an isolated group in service mode and cannot use the unsafe no-detach fallback.
- `src/process/supervisor/supervisor.test.ts` verifies the role is retained in run records and forwarded to the child adapter.
- `src/agents/cli-runner.spawn.test.ts` verifies both one-shot and Claude live CLI paths declare the executor role.

The preceding full run passed production types, test types, lint, core tests, CLI runner/tool shards, and agent runner shards. After rebasing onto current `main`, the fresh manual dispatch also exposed an unrelated existing `native:i18n:check` inventory drift; this PR does not touch native app or locale inventory paths. The PR-scoped CI remains the authoritative merge gate for the changed process, agent, gateway, and docs paths.

Local lightweight preflight: targeted `oxfmt`, targeted `oxlint`, `docs:map:check` against the same ClawHub docs source used by CI, and `git diff --check` all passed. Builds and full tests were intentionally run in GitHub Actions.

## Risk And Rollback

The behavior change is limited to process-supervisor ownership for CLI executors. Windows keeps its existing tree-termination path. POSIX background work retains the existing service-managed behavior. Reverting this commit restores the previous spawn policy and removes the role contract.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve target agent tool allowlist for subagents
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Spawned subagent sessions can lose tools that are allowed only on the target agent profile.

In the GBrain worker-read path, `main` can spawn `dennis-ritchie`, but `main` does not expose `gbrain_readonly`. Dennis has `tools.alsoAllow: ["gbrain_readonly"]`, yet the child session inherits the parent tool allowlist before the target-agent allowlist is persisted. The result is that a fresh Dennis worker does not receive the configured read-only tool even though the target agent configuration allows it.

## Fix

When creating the initial child session patch for `spawnSubagentDirect`, merge inherited tool allow entries from:

- the caller-provided inherited allowlist
- global subagent tool allowlist config: `tools.subagents.tools.alsoAllow`
- target agent config: `targetAgentConfig.tools.alsoAllow`

This keeps the allowlist scoped to the configured target agent instead of broadening the parent or global runtime tool policy.

## Evidence

Current rebased head:

```text
fcaaf7e31139a5ca4be4de43d1b6ca1afffab50f
```

Focused verification after rebasing onto current upstream `main`:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/agents/subagent-spawn.depth-limits.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts

Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       86 passed (86)
```

Additional checks:

```text
node --check src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts
git diff --check
```

The new regression coverage exercises `main -> dennis-ritchie` where the parent inherited tool allowlist lacks `gbrain_readonly`, but Dennis' target agent config includes `tools.alsoAllow: ["gbrain_readonly"]`; the persisted child session now retains `gbrain_readonly` in `inheritedToolAllow`.

## Real Runtime Reproduction

On the affected deployment after an approved gateway restart, a fresh real Dennis subagent still failed to receive the tool:

```text
Fresh Dennis subagent smoke:
- tool_search for gbrain_readonly returned 0 tools
- ALL_TOOLS had no gbrain/brain/readonly match
- stats/search/query/get_page checks could not run because the tool was absent
```

The gateway policy log for that same fresh Dennis spawn shows the exact failure mode:

```text
agents/tool-policy removed 17 tool(s) via tools.profile (coding): ...
agents/tool-policy removed 1 tool(s) via agents.dennis-ritchie.tools.deny: web_fetch
agents/tool-policy removed 7 tool(s) via subagent tools.deny: ...
agents/tool-policy removed 1 tool(s) via inherited tools: gbrain_readonly
```

The deployment config already grants Dennis and Albert `tools.alsoAllow` for `gbrain_readonly`, so this is not a missing config grant or plugin-load issue. The runtime is stripping the target-agent allowed tool from the child session through the inherited allowlist.

## Proof Boundary

Post-fix production proof requires this source fix to be merged/deployed and the protected gateway/runtime refresh to run. Until then, the only honest live proof available is the failure trace above plus the regression proving the fixed child-session envelope retains the target agent's configured allowlist.

## Scope

This PR is source-only. It does not deploy, change config, restart the gateway, or grant write/admin GBrain access.

target.title: fix(cron): persist startup catch-up deferrals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102236. A startup overflow catch-up slot could be persisted to SQLite while its protection marker existed only in memory. Restarting again before that slot fired let maintenance advance the job to its next natural cron slot, silently losing the deferred run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferral marker now lives on `CronJobState` as `pendingCatchupDeferral`, so the existing `state_json` persistence and rollback paths own the slot and marker together. The process-local Set and its parallel rollback bookkeeping are removed. Maintenance clears the persisted marker when the slot arrives, when no valid deferred slot remains, or when the job is disabled; execution also clears it after an outcome. Existing rows need no migration because an absent field means no pending deferral.

## User Impact

Overflow system-event cron jobs keep their staggered startup catch-up run across repeated gateway restarts instead of silently skipping to the next natural schedule. Unrelated stale future cron slots are still repaired normally.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite restart path: one service starts and persists an overflow deferral, a fresh service starts 3 seconds later against the same store, the original 5-second slot survives, executes once, and clears its marker.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.startup-overflow-clobber.test.ts src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts src/cron/service/ops.test.ts`: 3 files, 107 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.restart-catchup.test.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts`: 2 files, 81 tests passed.

target.title: fix(browser): check own profile entries for profile operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser profile names are user-controlled config keys. Inherited object properties such as `constructor` and `prototype` were treated as real profile entries in several create, delete, projection, hot-reload, and gateway patch paths. A valid profile with one of those names could therefore be rejected, omitted, or fail to round-trip.

Live route testing also exposed an adjacent deletion failure: when `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` or `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` placed Browser state outside the OS home/temp roots, deleting a launched profile returned HTTP 500 because the trash helper rejected Browser's own configured state directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use own-property checks at every Browser profile lookup boundary.
- Preserve valid top-level profile keys while continuing to strip nested prototype-pollution keys from untrusted config patches.
- Keep profile listing and hot reload consistent with persisted config.
- Authorize trash moves only from Browser's owned `<config>/browser` subtree. Existing realpath, symlink-escape, target-identity, and trash-destination checks remain in force; the wider config directory is not authorized.

## User Impact

Profiles named `constructor` or `prototype` can be created, listed, hot-reloaded, patched, and deleted normally. Custom state directories outside the home directory work without granting Browser deletion authority over unrelated config or filesystem paths.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `194d41eab680c1964c70087a60e03df607470878`
- Exact GitHub CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29032054298 - passed.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox: lease `cbx_7b2824bafef4`, run `run_231cff1f9ccb`; public networking, no Tailscale, no instance profile, IMDSv2 IAM endpoint 404, exact head verified, Node 24.15 / pnpm 11.2.2; 180 focused tests passed. Lease released.
- Native `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 scripts/pr prepare-run 101694` - passed at the exact PR head.
- Fresh autoreview at the exact head - clean, confidence 0.91.
- Real Express route proof: create and delete `constructor` through `POST /profiles/create` and `DELETE /profiles/constructor`; persistence round-tripped and `Object.prototype` remained unchanged.
- Real Gateway RPC proof: `config.patch` created and removed the profile while nested `constructor` / `prototype` payload keys remained stripped.
- Custom-state route proof: launched/stopped profile deletion under a configured state directory outside home/temp succeeds; unrelated config subtrees, root config authority, and symlink escapes remain rejected.

Live Dev Gateway + OpenAI agent + Browser proof will be added before merge; it is intentionally not claimed by the current evidence.

### 2026-07-12 follow-up: exact-head local proof

- Exact PR head verified locally: `ca0e4b3eff432c1c77cf5ae1810712c9e7570668`.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/profiles-service.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.hot-reload-profiles.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.list-profiles.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/trash.test.ts src/config/merge-patch.proto-pollution.test.ts src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts`.
- Result: passed 3 Vitest shards in 104.64s; 7 focused files passed; 139 tests passed.
- Coverage from the focused files: Browser profile own-entry create/list/hot-reload paths, prototype-like profile keys, trash authorization for Browser-owned state, nested prototype-pollution stripping in config merge patches, and Gateway `config.patch` behavior.
- This is exact-head local controlled proof. No live Dev Gateway, external provider, or browser UI session was exercised in this follow-up.

## Proof

### 2026-07-12 current-head local proof after update-branch

- Exact head tested: `c6055930d28aa0ecbe469406b0cdb60244a64526`
- Scope: Controlled local proof for browser profile own-entry operations on the current remote PR head. This covers profile service operations, browser server-context profile listing/hot reload behavior, trash handling, and adjacent config merge-patch pollution guards.

target.title: fix(openai): redact token refresh error response body
target.body:
﻿## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex OAuth token refresh reads the full error response body via `response.text()` on failed requests with no size limit and no redaction. Secrets in error responses (e.g. `refresh_token` in `error_description`) are exposed in the error message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the unbounded `response.text()` with `extractProviderErrorDetail` ? the canonical bounded provider error helper ? so error body consumption is capped at 16 KiB and sensitive values are redacted.

Matches the merged Chutes OAuth fix ([#103569](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103569)): `readResponseTextLimited` ? `assertOkOrThrowProviderError`, with secret redaction tests.

## User Impact

**Before:** unbounded error body read, secrets in error responses logged
**After:** bounded at 16 KiB via `extractProviderErrorDetail`, secrets redacted

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** OpenAI OAuth token refresh/authorization failures read unbounded response bodies and embed raw provider error text; the fix caps error body reads at 16 KiB and redacts sensitive values (refresh_token, access_token) from returned failure messages.

**Real environment tested:** Windows 11, Node.js v24.18.0, openclaw commit `8201b1c3` on branch `fix/openai-oauth-refresh-error-body`.

**Steps run after the patch:**
```
// Live loopback proof ? exercises extractProviderErrorDetail against real HTTP server
node --import tsx scripts/proof/openai-oauth-refresh-live.mts

// Full-chain regression tests ? exercises postTokenForm ? readResponseWithLimit ? extractProviderErrorDetail
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix:**
```
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof/openai-oauth-refresh-live.mts

=== #103578 bounded OAuth error proof ===

Case 1 ? secret redacted from error body: PASS
Case 2 ? oversized body bounded: PASS
Case 3 ? normal body preserved: PASS

OVERALL: ALL PASSED
```

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

**Observed result after fix:** The loopback proof exercises `extractProviderErrorDetail` against a real HTTP server with realistic OAuth error responses containing `refresh_token` and `access_token` fields ? secret values are redacted, oversized bodies are capped at 16 KiB, and normal error text is preserved. The regression tests exercise the full production `postTokenForm` ? `readResponseWithLimit` ? `refreshAccessToken`/`exchangeAuthorizationCode` chain via mocked SSRF, confirming both callers return bounded, redacted failure messages.

**What was not tested:** A live OAuth flow against the real `auth.openai.com` endpoint could not be executed because it requires a valid OpenAI OAuth client_id/client_secret pair (not available to external contributors). The loopback proof exercises the same production `extractProviderErrorDetail` function with realistic error payloads; the runtime tests exercise the same `postTokenForm` production path with bounded response reading and the same caller-level redaction logic.

## Diff summary

```
extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.ts      | 18 +/-
extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts | 101 ++++
scripts/proof/openai-oauth-refresh-live.mts                 |  89 ++++
```

- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
